criterion_notes.c1: Fails C1. Although municipal water rationing in Atenas County and concerns over future supply for the Tacares community water association (ASADA) formed the background to the disputed water-diversion infrastructure project ('Mejoras al Sistema de Abastecimiento de Atenas'), the study itself examines a socio-environmental conflict over spring water sources in Parque Recreativo Municipal Los Chorros and state-community political negotiation dynamics, rather than household or community water or sanitation service access (Exclusion Criterion 7).
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain/literal wording of Criterion 2, this paper would pass C2 ('yes') because it examines institutional and governance processes—specifically top-down public infrastructure policy implementation by the national water utility (AyA) and institutional conflict-resolution mechanisms (direct negotiation with a community technical commission and third-party facilitation by the Defensoría de los Habitantes). Under the active narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification, however, it fails C2 ('no') because it examines conflict management and citizen participation around an inter-canton water-capture infrastructure project rather than a rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, documentation or tenure rules for connections, administrative burden, tariffs/cost-recovery rules, enforcement/disconnection, or utility regulatory structure governing access). Incidental mentions of an amparo temporarily halting construction on environmental-viability grounds and park land tenure appear only as community protest tactics or negotiation agenda items, not analyzed service-access rules. Note that even under the plain reading of Criterion 2, overall full-text eligibility remains 'exclude' because C1 and C4 fail.
criterion_notes.c3: Meets C3. Qualitative empirical case study drawing on primary semi-structured interviews with Tacares community actors and institutional actors (including AyA leadership), supplemented by documentary review of institutional minutes and local and national media reports.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails C4. The empirical outcomes reported are political and conflict-negotiation outcomes—specifically the breakdown of consensus in direct negotiation and facilitated dialogue, the reproduction of power asymmetries (compelling residents to adopt technical language), the creation of AyA's social management unit in 2014, and the completion of the infrastructure project as originally designed in 2019. No empirical outcomes on household or community water access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion are measured or reported (the 2014 rationing figure in Atenas is cited only as background context from a newspaper article).
criterion_notes.c5: Meets C5 for its own research question. Qualitative single-case study design is identifiable, with identifiable collective/institutional actors (Tacares community members, Comisión Técnica Negociadora, Comité Pro Defensa del Agua del Parque Los Chorros, Municipality of Atenas, AyA, and Defensoría de los Habitantes; 4 cited key-informant interviews/communications from 2019 plus institutional records and media sources), conflict-resolution processes, and political negotiation outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Meets C6 via Criterion 10. Full text is in Spanish (with an English abstract); Spanish comprehension/translation from the provided full text is directly feasible, though the study is excluded on substantive scope grounds (C1, C2, C4).

evidence_quotes.quote: Para esto se caracterizan los actores presentes en las distintas negociaciones entre las partes, las estrategias empleadas en cada caso, y finalmente, la pertinencia o no de este tipo de respuestas institucionales para el procesamiento de demandas políticas ante un conflicto por el uso y gestión de un recurso natural de vital importancia: el agua.

En el artículo se analiza tanto el conflicto socioambiental como la búsqueda de una resolución negociada por parte del Estado. Para esto se emplea un diseño de investigación cualitativo a través de entrevistas semiestructuradas a actores de la comunidad de Tacares y a actores institucionales; asimismo se realiza una revisión bibliográfica de actas institucionales y de publicaciones en medios de comunicación locales y nacionales.

Para los vecinos de Tacares, la causa del conflicto era la implementación de un proyecto con las características de una política pública top-down pues la formulación y el inicio de su ejecución fue a través de una imposición institucional

Además, es posible apreciar cómo las distintas modalidades de resolución negociada reproducen asimetrías de poder en el seno de estos procesos. En este caso, un grupo de vecinos debió hacer amplios esfuerzos de coordinación para que sus propuestas fueran realmente escuchadas en las negociaciones, al punto de apelar a un lenguaje meramente técnico para el debate de sus demandas a través de la conformación de una comisión de este estricto carácter.

raw_response.exposure: Top-down implementation of an inter-canton water-capture infrastructure project by AyA and subsequent institutional conflict-negotiation processes (direct negotiation and third-party facilitation by the Defensoría de los Habitantes)
raw_response.outcome: Political conflict and negotiation outcomes: failure to ratify negotiated agreements, completion of the water transfer project as initially planned in 2019, reproduction of power asymmetries requiring community technical framing, and reactive promotion of citizen participation
raw_response.population_and_sample: Community actors in Tacares (Grecia canton) and institutional actors at the Instituto Costarricense de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AyA) involved in the 2012-2019 Parque Los Chorros water-source conflict (qualitative case study citing 4 interviews/personal communications in 2019, institutional minutes, and media reports; unit of analysis: conflict/negotiation episode and collective actors)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic), while also failing C2 (under the 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism scope) and C4 (no water service access outcome). This qualitative political-science case study analyzes community mobilization and state-led conflict-negotiation processes (direct negotiation and third-party facilitation) during a 2012-2019 socio-environmental conflict over spring water sources in Parque Recreativo Municipal Los Chorros (Tacares, Costa Rica). Although the disputed AyA infrastructure project was initiated to transfer water to Atenas County due to urban water shortages, the paper investigates natural-resource conflict resolution, political demand articulation, and power asymmetries at the negotiating table rather than household or community water service access (C1). It does not analyze any rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing service access (C2 narrow reading), and it reports no empirical outcomes on water access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion (C4). Consequently, both decision and plain_criterion2_decision are 'exclude'.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative case study (semi-structured interviews with community and institutional actors, institutional minutes, and media document analysis)
